questions.q: What happens to a user record when someone leaves the company?
options: It's permanently deleted from the org
It's automatically converted to a guest user
Nothing — Salesforce requires manual database cleanup
questions.explain: Salesforce never truly deletes a user; accounts are deactivated so historical data stays intact (covered fully in Lesson 3).

questions.q: Which button on the Users list page lets you create up to ten users at once?
questions.explain: Add Multiple Users opens a streamlined form for creating up to 10 user records in one pass.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four core building blocks of a user record?
questions.explain: The four building blocks are identity, license, profile, and role. Dashboards are a reporting feature, unrelated to user setup.

questions.q: A manager asks why a specific user can't see a report. Where should you check first?
options: The user's User Access Summary tab
questions.explain: User Access Summary lists every permission a specific user holds and where it came from, making it the fastest way to answer access questions.

questions.q: How many profiles can a single user be assigned at one time?
questions.explain: Every user must have exactly one profile, which sets their baseline permissions; additional access comes from permission sets and permission set groups.
